correctness.rationale: For 0<j<p, T^j−I=N u_j(N) with u_j(0)=j, giving the same kernel and image W as N. The group commutator in the stated convention is ((I−T^k)v+(T^j−I)w,0). It gives G'=W and lower central terms gamma_(r+1)=N^r V, so the class is exactly the maximum block length. The geometric-sum polynomial in characteristic p is (X−I)^(p−1), giving exponent p since (T^j−I)^(p−1)=0 and there are nonidentity vectors. Inside V the C_p-orbits are singleton or size p; outside V the translation conjugations give whole W-cosets and generator conjugation stays in each coset. Thus no outside element is central for N≠0, and the every-size class counts and center follow. In the dual of V, exactly p^b characters annihilate W and extend in p ways across the split cyclic quotient. The other orbits have size p; induction yields inequivalent irreducibles of degree p using restriction to V, and the degree-square sum is the order. For the word law, all nonzero quotient pairs produce a surjective linear map onto W, so uniform inputs give p^(−2) delta_0+(1−p^(−2)) U_W. Uniform measure is convolution-idempotent and the commutators are independent. This yields the stated exact fibers, including zero outside W. The two partitions have p parts totaling 2p, maximum lengths p−1 and 2, including at p=5, and hence meet every assumption. For the rank-one boundary, p=3 and n=2 give class counts 3 at size 1 and 8 at size 3, character counts 9 at 1 and 2 at 3, and one-commutator identity probability 11/27, consistent with 11 classes. evidence: The same-day pair in fact implies more than its printed surface-word comparison. For odd p write R=Z/p^k and α(j)=((1+p)^j−1)/p mod p^k. It is a bijection by v_p((1+p)^d−1)=1+v_p(d). For an element with a-coordinate x and cyclic coordinate j, the conjugacy class size is the size of the ideal generated by x mod p^k and α(j): the commuting condition with coordinates y,l is α(j)y=α(l)x in R, with equally many lifts of each residue. The corresponding Heisenberg condition is the alternating determinant on two coordinates of R², giving the very same class-size multiplicities. In each group each fixed coordinate pair has p^k lifts, so both centers have order p^k. On the metacyclic dual of <a>, for d≥1 there are (p−1)p^d characters of orbit length p^d; each orbit has p^(k−d) extensions to its split stabilizer, and the extra abelian factor multiplies the degree-p^d count by p^(k−1). This gives (p−1)p^(2k−d−1). In H_k, the abelian normal R² has p^k characters per fixed central character and orbit size p^d if that central character has order p^d. Induction from the split stabilizer gives p^(2(k−d)) irreducibles per such central character. Multiplying by phi(p^d) gives the same count; each group has p^(2k) linears from the quotient by its derived group.

value.rationale: The exponent-p restriction is structural, not an arbitrary slice: it removes the cyclic prime-power mechanism and tests blindness without higher element orders or cyclic derived groups supplying class information. The example shows that rank alone controls all these distributions while the length of the Jordan filtration governs nilpotency class, even with a class-two comparator and class approaching p. This gives a usable obstruction for reconstructing class in a natural and narrower group family than the cyclic cousins.
residual_risks: The gap is not unbounded at fixed p in the frozen construction. No assertion about arbitrary words, full character tables or reconstruction from finer data.
